rounds.restatement: Values reach the template resolver from n8n as strings. The card fixes two defects in how those strings are coerced. First, repairing a JSON object or array string must remove only structural commas (leading, trailing, doubled) and must never rewrite commas inside string literals. Second, a numeric path segment on a string input (tags.0) must index through the same array coercion FOR uses, so that both 'a,b' and '["a","b"]' index like arrays, in ${{...}} output and in IF conditions. The change must not alter any other behavior, edit existing tests or add a runtime dependency. It serves a cycle goal of fixing the Tier 0 bugs while keeping the core pure and CI green.

rounds.restatement: Values reach the template resolver from n8n as strings. Two things must hold. First, when the resolver repairs a JSON object or array string, it removes only structural stray commas (leading, trailing, doubled) and never changes a comma inside a string value. Second, a path such as tags.0 on a string input uses the same coercion FOR uses, so 'a,b' and '["a","b"]' index like arrays in both ${{...}} output and IF conditions. Nothing else may change behavior, no existing test may be edited or deleted, and no runtime dependency may be added. The work has to stay inside coercion.ts, expressions.ts and interpreter.ts.

findings.title: Conditions lose non-numeric property access on JSON-array strings (for example tags.length), a behavior change outside the named defects

serves.scenario: Before the change, expressions.resolveValue ran JSON.parse on any string intermediate, so with tags='["a","b"]' a condition such as {{IF tags.length > 1}} reached the parsed array and could read its 'length' property. After the change, tryCoerceStringForPathSegment returns null for a non-numeric segment on a string that is not an object, so resolveValue returns null. The ordering comparison then throws TypeError, or == yields a different result. No defect named in the card asks for this change.

findings.rubric: no change outside the card scope / must not change behavior outside the named defects
findings.reproduction: With base e7069db and head 2a63dc1, run resolveTemplate('{{IF tags.length > 1}}Y{{ELSE}}N{{END_IF}}', new Map([['tags','["a","b"]']]), {strictMode:false}). This holds if the lookup code after the string branch in resolveValue resolves own or array properties such as 'length', which is plausible because it previously received the JSON.parse result unchanged. Expect 'Y' at base and a thrown TypeError, or 'N', at head. The smallest fix: in resolveValue, keep the old JSON.parse result as a fallback when tryCoerceStringForPathSegment returns null, or apply the array coercion only for numeric segments and otherwise keep the JSON.parse behavior.

findings.title: Conditions now repair malformed object strings, and array repair now also collapses comma runs in the middle of an array and commas after '{'

serves.scenario: In IF conditions, '{"a":1,}' used to fail JSON.parse and give null; it now repairs and resolves. In tryCoerceToArray, '["a",,"b"]' used to fail JSON.parse and fall back to comma splitting; it now parses as ["a","b"]. Both changes follow the card's goal that one coercion serves everywhere and that only structural commas are repaired, so neither needs a fix. They are behavior changes the lead may want recorded.

findings.rubric: no change outside the card scope
findings.reproduction: Run {{IF o.a == 1}}Y{{ELSE}}N{{END_IF}} with o='{"a":1,}' (base: N, head: Y). Run {{FOR a AS x}}[${{x}}]{{END_FOR}} with a='["a",,"b"]' and compare base with head.
findings.label: f2

rulings.note: intended consequence of one structural-comma repair everywhere; recorded

findings.title: Array-string repair now also collapses doubled commas between elements, which changes FOR/index results for inputs like '[1,,2]'

serves.scenario: At base, tryCoerceToArray stripped only ',]' and '[,' from a '['-prefixed string. '[1,,2]' therefore failed JSON.parse and fell back to comma splitting, which gives string pieces. At head, repairStructuralCommas also collapses the doubled comma, so JSON.parse succeeds and gives the numbers [1,2]. Rendered FOR output is the same. Type-sensitive checks on items, or JSON output of an indexed sub-array, could differ. This is a small widening beyond the named defects. It is not a criterion failure.

findings.rubric: no change outside the card scope
findings.reproduction: Run resolveTemplate('{{FOR a AS x}}{{IF x isNumber}}N{{ELSE}}S{{END_IF}}{{END_FOR}}', new Map([['a','[1,,2]']]), {strictMode:false}) at base and at head, and compare. The results differ only if isNumber distinguishes a numeric string from a number.
findings.label: f3
